allocations.exactDerivedText: Calls to slow the most powerful AI
Anthropic’s chief proposed slower capability gains and outside safety reviewers; an industry-wide agreement is not in place.

On September 12, Anthropic chief Dario Amodei called for slowing improvements to the most capable AI systems so safety work can keep up. He is not proposing an end to model development. Anthropic’s own commitment is to invite outside reviewers with ongoing access similar to staff who assess risk.

His proposed arrangement includes access to relevant workspaces and tools, with privacy, legal and contractual exceptions. Reviewers would be able to publish findings without Anthropic’s editorial control, subject to narrow redactions, and say if a redaction affected their conclusions.
It remains a commitment to put a system in place, not evidence that the reviewers are already operating. Wider limits would require cooperation across companies and governments.
outside-review arrangements
Dario Amodei — We Must Pace the Frontier
a disturbing misuse report

Anthropic’s September 10 threat report describes concerning uses of its systems, including surveillance and biological research with potential for harm. These are the company’s findings about activity it observed, not a measure of all AI use.
The biological examples do not establish a completed weapon, and the report does not assert that the scientists intended harm.
Anthropic — September threat report
school privacy terms
School AI privacy protections have a contract behind them, but schools must opt in and product exclusions matter.

Microsoft, the American Federation of Teachers and the United Federation of Teachers announced school AI privacy terms on September 9. The signed agreement gives US schools a route to request protections for covered educational AI products.
Coverage is not automatic. Schools must opt in, and the definition excludes general-purpose productivity, communications and search products even when schools use them.

Google announced new live voice models

Google announced Gemini 3.8 Live and Live Extended Thinking on September 15. It says the models can continue a spoken conversation while processing tasks in the background. The first is rolling out in Search Live; Extended Thinking is rolling out in Gemini Live. Its Docs features require Google AI Pro or Ultra; Gmail and Keep features require a Google AI subscription.
Availability still depends on the rollout and the feature.
Google — Gemini 3.8 Live announcement
OpenAI is testing conversations sponsored by advertisers.
On September 16, OpenAI announced it is testing an optional, separately labelled advertiser-sponsored chat after an ad click in ChatGPT, with select US advertisers.
That is a seller’s conversation.

funding arrangements

After this roundup’s covered week, Anthropic named Accenture as an evaluation partner, with the work led by its Faculty business. Anthropic will pay for that work directly. The company says access and reporting standards are still unsettled. Naming a partner is a step beyond the earlier promise; it is not a completed independent assessment.
